parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
An ideal gas is assumed to consist of atoms or molecules that behave as hard, identical
spheres that are in continuous motion and undergo elastic collisions.
State two further assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases.

markscheme_points.text: e.g. time of collisions negligible compared to time between collisions no intermolecular forces (except during collisions) random motion (of molecules) large numbers of molecules (total) volume of molecules negligible compared to volume of containing vessel or average/mean separation large compared with size of molecules any two

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the mass of one atom of helium-4 is $6.6 \times 10^{-24}\,\mathrm{g}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
mass = 4.0 / (6.02 × 10 23) = 6.6 × 10-24 g or mass = 4.0 × 1.66 × 10-27 × 103 = 6.6 × 10-24 g
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The mean kinetic energy $E_{\mathrm{K}}$ of an atom of an ideal gas is given by the expression
$$E_{\mathrm{K}} = \frac{3}{2}kT.$$
Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed of a helium-4 atom at a temperature of $27\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
$$\text{r.m.s. speed} = \text{................................................... }\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in ideal gas laws and thermodynamics connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:

State the core physical principle governing this problem: Ideal gas laws and thermodynamics. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
2 3 kT = 2 1 m <c 2>
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
